assessments.explanation: The paragraph describes the Board's finding of inadmissibility based on misrepresentation about marital history.
The paragraph details Mr. Baro’s admission of a previous marriage and the circumstances surrounding his failure to disclose it.
The paragraph outlines Mr. Baro’s appeal to the IAD and the issues on judicial review, including the standard of reasonableness.
The paragraph recounts Mr. Baro’s marriage to Elizabeth Gandeza and his subsequent loss of contact.
The paragraph explains Mr. Baro’s relationship with Ms. Tuzon and his marriage to her after presumed death of his first wife.
The paragraph describes Mr. Baro’s application for Canadian permanent residence and the omission of his prior marriage in official documents.
The paragraph details how Ms. Tuzon discovered Mr. Baro’s first marriage and the subsequent allegations of misrepresentation.
The paragraph summarizes the Board’s conclusion that Mr. Baro misrepresented facts by providing false documentation and omitting material information.
The paragraph explains the IAD’s findings that Mr. Baro knowingly submitted inaccurate information and failed to disclose material facts.
The paragraph states that the court can only overturn the IAD’s decision if it was unreasonable.
The paragraph discusses Mr. Baro’s argument that the IAD erred in assessing his credibility regarding the certificate.
The paragraph concludes that there is no contradiction in Mr. Baro’s testimony and the IAD’s credibility finding was unfounded.
The paragraph notes that the Board’s finding of failure to disclose marital history is unaffected by its erroneous finding about Mr. Baro’s intent.
The paragraph discusses the absence of the application form and the question of whether Mr. Baro had a duty to disclose his marital history.
The paragraph explains the statutory duty to disclose material facts under IRPA and relevant case law on innocent failures.
The paragraph states that marital history is relevant to spousal sponsorship applications and the importance of genuine relationships.
The paragraph emphasizes that applicants cannot anticipate all relevant information and must consider circumstances.
The paragraph concludes that Mr. Baro was obliged to disclose his marital history given the officials’ request and his conduct.
The paragraph states that the IAD’s decision was reasonable regarding Mr. Baro’s failure to disclose material facts under s. 40(1)(a).
The paragraph notes Mr. Baro’s argument that the IAD erred on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, though he did not press this point strongly.
The paragraph describes Mr. Baro’s submission about the impact on his parents if he were removed from Canada.
The paragraph reports the IAD’s consideration of Mr. Baro’s parents’ situation and its conclusion that there was insufficient evidence of dependency.
The paragraph states that the court finds no reason to overturn the IAD’s conclusion on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
The paragraph states that the application for judicial review is dismissed and no questions are certified for appeal.
